newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Four killed, seven hurt in road crash in Bulgaria.
newsitem.headline: Four killed, seven hurt in road crash in Bulgaria.

text.p: Three East European tourists and a Bulgarian were killed when a tourist bus and a fuel tanker collided near the northeastern Bulgarian town of Shumen on Wednesday, a senior traffic police officer said.

"All we know now is that the three dead tourists are either Belarus or Ukraine citizens: an eight-year-old girl called Tasha, Dmitrii, who was about 35, and Vladimir Kernidskiy, 43," the officer from the Shumen police department told Reuters by telephone.
The fourth victim was the driver of the Bulgarian-registered bus, which is owned by Bulgarian tourist firm Riki-A. The accident occured on Wednesday morning as the bus headed for the Black Sea coast.
Six other foreign passengers and one Bulgarian were being treated in hospital in Shumen, the police officer said.
"Three of the injured are in a critical condition. Among them are two women from Belarus -- Alla Kernidskaya and Lyubov Domenchuk," he said.
He gave no details of the accident but state radio said that the bus driver had apparently swerved to avoid pedestrians only to end up in the same lane as the oncoming Mercedes tanker truck.
